data.turoyo: Komər qayimo, mčakčakla droʕona w nafilo bi baxča, d maḥišola remune w ṭaʕmone.
data.translation: Sie krempelte ihre Ärmel auf und machte sich über den Garten her, um sich Granatäpfel und allerhand Früchte zu pflücken.

rationale: Fill Infectum 1 with a feminine subject, explicit pomegranates/fruit objects and a beneficiary co-referential with the picker.

summary: The woman picks named fruits for herself (maḥišola, 105/100), while the man offers to pick for her with -lax (105/102, /105). The ordinary beneficiary suffix can be co-referential with the subject or refer to another person.
An overt fruit object and an understood fruit object alternate within the same III.1 meaning. The purpose d-clause and prospective g- differ in discourse without a new lexical sense.
All three supplied occurrences are Infectum. The Preterit base in the inherited form line is not treated as a newly attested box, and the repeated offer is not added solely to increase counts.
No specialized idiom or light-verb collocation is established.
